title: Peanut Butter and Jelly Sandwich on Wheat Bread

content.title: About
content.content: The sandwich consists of two slices of wheat bread, a thin layer of reduced‑fat peanut butter, and sweet fruit jelly. It is a classic American snack that combines protein, carbohydrates, and a modest amount of fat.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Reduced‑fat peanut butter typically contains about 30 % fat instead of the 50 % found in regular versions.
Wheat bread retains more fiber and micronutrients than white bread.
The peanut butter & jelly sandwich appeared in the United States in the early 20th century and gained popularity after World War II.
The sweet‑salty flavor balance is considered ideal by many nutritionists.
Some U.S. schools ban peanut butter sandwiches because of allergy concerns.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: Peanut butter provides about 8 g of protein per serving, supporting muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Contains heart‑healthy monounsaturated fats
items.content: Even with reduced fat, the remaining monounsaturated fats can help maintain cardiovascular health.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Wheat bread adds fiber that promotes healthy digestion.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Both the bread and the jelly supply thiamine, riboflavin, and niacin, which are essential for energy metabolism.

items.title: Lower glycemic impact with no‑added‑sugar jelly
items.content: Choosing a jelly without added sugar results in a more moderate blood‑sugar response compared with conventional jams.

items.title: Peanut allergy
items.content: Peanut butter can trigger severe allergic reactions in susceptible individuals.

items.title: Sugar content in jelly
items.content: Traditional jelly often contains a lot of added sugar, increasing calories and affecting glucose levels.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Even with reduced fat, the sandwich remains relatively calorie‑dense; portion size should fit within daily energy goals.

items.title: Sodium in reduced‑fat peanut butter
items.content: Some low‑fat versions add salt; those monitoring sodium intake should choose a no‑salt option.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Spread a thin layer of peanut butter on one slice of bread, evenly spread jelly on the other, and press together. The sandwich is easy to eat by hand, or cut into halves or quarters for children.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the assembled sandwich in an airtight container at room temperature for no more than 4 hours. Store opened peanut butter and jelly in the refrigerator, and keep bread in a dry place.
